data.raw_text:
Congratulations to everyone who showed up today in Forbes Park.

Let me just share a widely studied principle in political science called the “3.5% rule.”

According to research, history shows that when around 3.5% of a nation’s population consistently participates in protests, that movement almost always succeeds in forcing real change.

For the Philippines, that’s roughly 4 million people.

But here’s the key part: they don’t have to protest all at once or in one place. That number refers to collective and sustained participation — people across the country taking part in waves, over weeks or months, through rallies, strikes, organizing, and civic actions.

It’s about building steady pressure.

So today matters. Every action adds up. Every gathering contributes to that momentum. What counts is not just the size of one protest, but the persistence of many.

And as the country’s situation grows more fragile by the day — especially with the impending economic winter — I can only see these protests gaining strength in the coming weeks and months.

Traffic Advisory
Day 14, Monday 13th October, 2025

Design and construction of Residences for the Head of Courts (President, Court of Appeal; Federal High Court Chief Judge; Chief Judge of the FCT, Abuja; and President Industrial Court)

The attention of the FCT motoring public are hereby drawn to the movement of dignitaries to the venue of the event at AIG Ali Amodu Crescent, opposite Abacha Barrack.

Traffic will be slightly affected at the AYA roundabout, Lisa Suites, James Ogbede Crescent and other nearby locations.

Security and traffic personnel will be deployed at 0800hrs accordingly to give direction and equally ensure seamless traffic flow, especially areas with traffic bottlenecks.

- Head Traffic, DRTS
